terms.meaning: A reusable piece of a web page, written in code, that shows some content.
The large top section of a page, usually with a headline and main picture.
A display setting. Here the hero shows an animation instead of a photo.
The rule that matches a web address to the page that should show for it.

sections.name: File setup, BUILD_FOCUS
sections.title: Imports and build focus map
sections.what: Brings in the pieces this page needs and maps each of the four tools to the part of the dark-mode animation that should be highlighted.
sections.why: Likely reason: each tool's animation should point at the part of the process that matches that tool.
sections.watch_out: The map only has the four tool keys, so a new tool gets no highlight until it is added here.

sections.name: IntelligenceFooter
sections.title: Shared page footer
sections.what: Shows the brand name, the subtitle Capital Projects Intelligence, and a confidentiality line, all taken from the brand settings.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared footer keeps every landing page looking the same.
sections.watch_out: The footer text comes from the brand settings, so a brand change alters every landing page that uses it.

sections.name: ToolLanding
sections.title: Landing page for one tool
sections.what: Builds the full landing page for whichever tool the address points to. It shows a hero, buttons to open the workspace and view a demo or workflow, the steps, the output and caveat, and links to the other tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: one reusable page for four tools keeps them consistent, with the text coming from the content file.
sections.watch_out: If the address matches no tool, it silently shows the first tool, which can hide a broken link.

summary: Builds the landing page for each of the four intelligence tools, with a hero, workflow steps, an output note, and links to the other tools.
purpose: Gives each tool a consistent entry page that explains it and links to its workspace.
why: Likely reason: one page template for all four tools keeps them consistent, with the wording coming from each tool's entry in the content file.
how: Reads the current address to find the matching tool. Shows a hero with a dark-mode animation or a photo, the tool's headline, and buttons to open the workspace and view a demo or the workflow. Then lists the steps, the output description with its caveat, and links to the other tools. Shows the footer that suits the tool.
inputs: The current page address and search string, plus the tool list from the content file and the dark mode setting.
outputs: A full landing page shown in the browser. No data is saved.
risks: If the address matches no tool, the first tool appears silently, which can hide a wrong link. The opportunity tool has a different footer disclaimer that must stay accurate.
debug: If the wrong tool shows, compare the address with the tool's path in the content file. If a button is missing, check the tool's demo and guide fields. If the hero is blank, check the image path and the dark mode setting.
